pr_title: sql/schemachanger: disable CREATE SEQUENCE / CREATE SCHEMA by default in declarative schema changer
pr_body:
For 23.2 and keeping things more conservative, we will keep CREATE SEQUENCE / CREATE SCHEMA running
in the older declarative schema changer. This patch will do the following:

1. CREATE SEQUENCE / CREATE SCHEMA are disabled by default
2. A new cluster setting sql.schema.force_declarative_statements can now be used to enable/disable declarative features in a more granular matter.


Fixes: #107734
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/107815)

issue_context.title: sql/schemachanger: disable CREATE SEQUENCE / CREATE SCHEMA in declarative schema changer
issue_context.body:
We should disable CREATE SEQUENCE / CREATE SCHEMA until improved test coverage is in place. Additionally, let's introduce a cluster setting for more *granular* disablement of features, so that if/when bugs are found, users are not forced to flip a big switch.

Jira issue: CRDB-30176

review_comments:
The type -> tag mapping already exists by calling `tree.Statement.StatemengTag()`. For this change, we just need to have a `map[string]struct{}` of supported values to know what the user is allowed to set.

If we have test cases for each of these statement types that test the correct `fn`, `on`, and `checks` behavior, then we do not need `type supportedStatement struct` and `supportedStatements` can be replaced with type switches. The type switches will remove the need for reflection in order to call `fn` or `checks`.

I think we need to have these test cases anyways to check that the builder function `fn` can be called, the default state of `on`, the branches in `checks`, and that the default state can be overridden by the new setting.

So, the scbuild tests will use unsafe_always options and cover the entire set of statements in this array. I think reflection is cleaner in this case, using type switches will mean multiple switches for these structures and it's just cleaner to not repeat things. i.e. We need to be able to execute Check vs Build callbacks, and properties for each statement.

If we want to explore a different structure for the existing stuff lets leave it for a different PR
We spoke about this offline and will address the reflection separately.
